html:
The mutilation of the herms was an act of vandalism in Athens one night in 415 BCE, just before the fleet sailed on the Sicilian Expedition. Almost all the herms of the city were smashed.

A herm was a stone pillar topped with a head of the god Hermes, with male genitals carved on the front. Herms stood at house doors, gateways and crossroads to bring luck and protect travellers. Damaging them all at once looked like a terrible omen for the expedition, and many Athenians feared it was part of a plot to overthrow the democracy.

The city offered rewards, and informers came forward. Some of them also charged that the Eleusinian Mysteries had been mocked in private houses, and they named Alcibiades. He was allowed to sail, then recalled to stand trial. He escaped on the way home and fled to Sparta, and Athens sentenced him to death in his absence. The orator Andocides confessed to save himself and named others. Who really smashed the herms, and why, has never been settled.
